editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CET on 31 October; new research covers 05:10 CET to 17:10 CET on 31 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Ukraine Says Neptune Missiles and Drones Struck a Rocket Fuel Plant in Russia
items.lede: Kyiv's General Staff reported a warehouse fire and four damaged workshops at the Rostov-region plant, which it says fuels Russian rocket launchers.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Kamensky Combine in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, in Russia's Rostov region, on the night of 30–31 October [1]. It said strike drones and Navy-operated Neptune coastal missiles were used [1]. The General Staff said a fire broke out at a finished-products warehouse and four production workshops were damaged [1]. It said the plant makes solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S rocket launchers and for other missiles [1]. Four Russian military supply depots in occupied parts of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Luhansk regions were also hit, it said [1]. No Russian official comment on the plant was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the strike and damage rest on Ukraine's General Staff claim, carried by one Ukrainian outlet, with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Ukraine Downs 105 of 134 Russian Drones Launched Overnight Into Saturday
items.lede: Twenty locations were still hit and some drones remained airborne Saturday morning, the Air Force said in a preliminary count.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 134 attack drones from 18:00 Kyiv time on Friday 30 October (17:00 CET) [2]. It said 72 of the Shahed drones were jet-powered, and Gerbera and decoy drones were also used [2]. The drones came from Oryol, Kursk, Shatalovo, and Millerovo in Russia, and from occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske in Crimea [2]. As of 08:30 Kyiv time (07:30 CET) on Saturday, air defenses had shot down or jammed 105 drones [2]. Drones hit 20 locations, debris fell at 10 more, and several drones were still in the air [2]. No Russian Defense Ministry figure for the same night was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the totals, because they are the Air Force's own preliminary figures, carried here by a single Ukrainian outlet.

items.title: Erdoğan Hosts Zelensky in Istanbul for Talks on War and Black Sea
items.lede: Ukraine's and Turkey's intelligence chiefs joined the delegation talks at Dolmabahçe, and a joint news conference was expected afterward.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will make a working visit to Istanbul on 31 October at President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's invitation, Turkish presidential communications head Burhanettin Duran said on X [3][4]. Duran said the talks would cover bilateral cooperation, the war between Russia and Ukraine, and the security situation in the Black Sea [3][4]. Ukrinform noted that Türkiye has said it is ready to help arrange a leaders' meeting to end the war [3]. Zelensky arrived in Istanbul on Saturday, and Turkish Defense Minister Yaşar Güler met him at the airport [5]. Erdoğan received him at the Dolmabahçe presidential office, and the two leaders held one-on-one talks [6][5]. Güler, Turkish intelligence chief İbrahim Kalın, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, and foreign intelligence head Rustem Umierov joined the delegation talks [6]. Zelensky said on X that commercial shipping in the Black Sea raised significant issues [5]. A joint news conference was expected after the meeting, and no outcome had been reported by the cutoff [5].
Confidence is high that the meeting took place, because the Turkish presidency's press service and a Turkish and a Ukrainian outlet report it. No outcome is established yet.

items.title: Fire Hits Refinery in Russia's Ufa as Airports Close Under Drone Threat
items.lede: Moscow's mayor said 11 drones were downed near the capital on Saturday, while local officials in Bashkortostan stayed silent on the blasts.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Russia's aviation agency Rosaviatsia imposed temporary flight restrictions at Kazan and Samara airports early on Saturday 31 October, Interfax reported [7]. Restrictions followed at Yekaterinburg and Perm airports in the Urals around 04:00 CET, Interfax said [8]. Rosaviatsia gave no reason in the messages quoted [7][8]. Such restrictions usually accompany Ukrainian drone raids, but no drone attack on these regions was confirmed in the reports read by the cutoff. Residents of Ufa, capital of Russia's Bashkortostan region, reported explosions overnight and smoke over an industrial area on Saturday morning, BBC News Russian said, as relayed by Ukrinform [9]. Rosaviatsia closed Ufa airport around 04:00 local time (00:00 CET), and it stayed closed, the report said [9]. Astra's analysts said a key reforming unit at the Bashneft-Novoil refinery was on fire [9]. Local authorities made no statement [9]. On Saturday afternoon, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 11 drones were shot down on approach to the capital [10]. Astra reported a forest fire north of Sheremetyevo Airport near its fuel complex [10].

Confidence is moderate. The closures rest on Rosaviatsia notices relayed by Interfax, and the Ufa and Sheremetyevo fires rest on Telegram channel Astra and BBC News Russian relayed by Ukrinform. No official Russian confirmation of a strike on the refinery was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Kremlin Says Abu Dhabi Talks With Ukraine and the U.S. Carry No Truce Pledge
items.lede: Lavrov later invited Zelensky to Moscow with Russian security guarantees and rejected a report that Moscow wants a phone call instead of a face-to-face meeting.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday that preparing for three-way talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi does not commit Russia to limit fighting. He said Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries do not affect those talks [11]. He repeated that Russia opposes a ceasefire that would give Ukrainians a breather [11]. Asked about a Putin–Zelensky call, Peskov said Putin was open to dialogue and no one had called yet [12]. The Kyiv Independent, citing an unnamed senior Ukrainian official, reported that Kyiv suspects Moscow of offering a phone call to avoid an in-person leaders' meeting [12]. Late Friday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told a news conference in Atlanta that if Zelensky wants to meet Putin, he can come to Moscow [13]. Lavrov said Russia would guarantee Zelensky's security there and that whoever requests a meeting must accept the host's terms [13]. Asked by Deutsche Welle about the Kyiv Independent report, Lavrov rejected the idea that the Kremlin wants a phone call rather than an in-person meeting [14][15]. No report gave a date for the Abu Dhabi round [11][12][13].

Confidence is high on Peskov's and Lavrov's statements, which Interfax, the Kyiv Independent, and DW carry on record. Kyiv's suspicion of a phone-call ploy rests on one outlet and an anonymous official.

items.title: Last Oleshky Evacuee Plane Lands in Belarus on the Way to Ukraine
items.lede: Arakhamia said the evacuees and Kyiv's delegation would cross into Ukrainian-held land within hours, though no headcount has been published.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia have observed a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, since 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET) [16][17]. U.S. First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [18][19], and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [20]. Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets had said residents could leave until 14:00 local time, with aid handouts due to start after 14:30 [21][22]. On Friday Lubinets and Russia's ombudsman Yana Lantratova ran the joint mission, and Arakhamia said aid had been delivered [23][24][25]. Arakhamia said evacuees would travel via Anapa, Russia, and Belarus to Ukraine [25]. On Friday evening Lubinets said those wishing to go to Ukraine had left Oleshky and were on their way, with no ceasefire violations in 87 hours [26]. Interfax, citing Russian TV channel Zvezda, said evacuated residents were taken to a temporary shelter in Simferopol, in occupied Crimea [27]. On Saturday, Arakhamia said the final plane had landed in Gomel, Belarus [28]. He said evacuees and the delegation would reach Ukraine within hours [28].

Confidence is high that evacuees left, because Ukrainian and Russian officials say so on record. The headcount, the Simferopol detail from Russian state TV, and arrival in Ukraine are not established.

items.title: Russian Strike on Kyiv Energy Site Cuts Power to Four Districts
items.lede: The Left Bank lost running water after three drones hit critical infrastructure, Mayor Klitschko said, with no casualties confirmed by early Saturday.

sections.text: A Russian attack hit an energy facility in Ukraine's capital Kyiv on the evening of Friday 30 October. The strike cut electricity to parts of the Obolonskyi, Darnytskyi, Desnianskyi, and Podilskyi districts, energy company DTEK said [29][30]. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram that three drone strikes hit critical infrastructure and that the city's Left Bank was without water [30]. He said water pressure had dropped across the supply system while energy workers restored power [29]. Kyiv Independent staff reported explosions and power fluctuations across the city [30]. There were no confirmed reports of casualties when the Kyiv Independent published, and the full extent of the damage was unclear [30].
Confidence is high that an energy site was hit and districts lost power and water, because DTEK and the mayor say so on record, reported by two Ukrainian outlets. The damage is not yet assessed.

items.title: U.S. Clears Possible $2.1 Billion Sale of 500 Patriot Interceptors to Ukraine
items.lede: Allies would fund the missiles, but Zelensky warned delivery could take years and asked partners for interceptors from existing stocks before winter.

sections.text: The U.S. State Department on Friday approved a possible $2.1 billion sale to Ukraine of 500 PAC-3 MSE interceptors for Patriot air defense systems. The package includes spare parts and support [31][32]. Canada, Germany, and Norway would pay through the JUMPSTART program, alongside Ukrainian funds from the EU's Ukraine Support Loan, with no U.S. money [31][32]. Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor [31]. No delivery timeline was given, and Congress generally has 30 days to review such a sale [32]. Zelensky welcomed the decision but warned deliveries could take years, and urged partners to send interceptors from existing stocks now [32]. NATO's top commander, General Alexus Grynkewich, said in Riga that allied-funded deliveries were continuing without delays, Bloomberg reported [32].
Confidence is high on the approval and its terms, because two outlets report the State Department's notice. Delivery timing is not established.

items.title: Russia Fires 113 Drones and 17 Ballistic Missiles at Ukraine Into Friday
items.lede: Ninety-nine aerial targets were downed or jammed, but 17 sites were hit, and Zelensky said scarce Patriot interceptors make ballistic missiles harder to stop.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia attacked from 18:00 Kyiv time on Thursday 29 October (17:00 CET). It said Russia used Iskander-M, S-400, and KN-23 ballistic missiles, four Kh-59/69 guided missiles, and 113 attack drones, 83 of them jet-powered [33]. As of 07:30 Kyiv time (06:30 CET) on Friday it said 99 targets were shot down or suppressed: three guided missiles and 96 drones [33]. Hits were recorded at 17 locations and debris fell at five more, with Kyiv, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk regions the main targets [33]. The Air Force did not give the number of ballistic missiles, but President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his Friday evening address that Russia launched 17 overnight [33][34]. He said ballistic missiles are harder to stop, especially with Patriot interceptors in short supply, and that Russia had taken no step toward energy de-escalation [34]. No Russian Defense Ministry figure for the same night was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the totals, because they are the Air Force's and the president's own figures, carried here by a single Ukrainian outlet.

items.title: Ukraine Seeks Emergency UN Security Council Session Over Deadly Strikes
items.lede: Kyiv's envoy Andrii Melnyk cited 20 civilians killed in three cities and urged members to expel Russia, though no session date was set.

sections.text: Ukraine's UN ambassador Andrii Melnyk said on Friday 30 October that Ukraine is convening an emergency UN Security Council meeting after Russian attacks on Dnipro, Chernihiv, and Kremenchuk [35][36]. He wrote on X that Russian strikes there had killed 20 civilians and wounded dozens more, adding "Kick Russia out" [35][36]. A strike on Dnipro railway station on 29 October killed at least 15 people, Chernihiv lost two 15-year-old girls, and three people died in Kremenchuk [36][35]. Local authorities put the toll from Russian attacks across Ukraine over the preceding day at 27 killed and 128 injured [36]. No meeting date was given in either report.
Confidence is high that Ukraine requested the meeting, because Melnyk said so on record, reported by two Ukrainian outlets. The casualty totals are local officials' figures.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Stray Drone Forces Moldova to Close Northern and Central Airspace
items.lede: The unidentified drone crossed from Ukraine's Odesa region during Russian strikes on Ukraine and vanished from radar about 30 minutes later.

sections.text: An unauthorized drone entered Moldova's airspace on Saturday at 15:24 CET, Moldova's Air Operations Center said [1][2]. It came from the direction of Semionovca in Ukraine's Odesa region and headed toward Plopi in the Transnistrian region [1][2]. Radar later tracked it near Bănești in Telenești district [2]. Moldova restricted airspace in the north at 15:46 CET and in the center at 15:52 CET [2]. The drone disappeared from radar near Țibirica in Călărași district at 15:54 CET [1][2]. Authorities reopened northern and central airspace at 16:14 CET after the drone left Moldovan airspace [1]. The Defense Ministry linked the incident to massive Russian attacks on Ukraine [1]. Officials warned residents to stay at least 500 meters from any debris and call 112 [1][2]. No damage, injuries, or drone type had been reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the route, the airspace closures, and the timeline, which MOLDPRES and TVR Moldova both reported from Moldova's Defense Ministry. The drone's type and origin were not officially named.

items.title: Jersey Police Hunt Drone Operators After Flights From Britain Divert
items.lede: Officers believe two or three unauthorized drones were involved, see no terrorism link, and are asking residents of the island's west for footage.

sections.text: Unauthorized drones flew in restricted airspace near Jersey Airport on Friday evening, disrupting flights from Britain to the British Crown Dependency [3]. The first report came at about 20:20 local time (21:20 CET), and further drone activity was reported until about 22:30 (23:30 CET) [4]. Three inbound flights from London Gatwick, London Heathrow, and Southampton were diverted [3]. The Gatwick flight landed at about 23:45 GMT (00:45 CET Saturday), and the Heathrow and Southampton services were canceled [3]. Jersey Police Inspector Rob McCallum said officers believed two or three drones had been in the restricted airspace [3]. He said the incident was not thought to be linked to terrorism [3]. Police searched several areas in the west of the island but had not identified an operator [4]. Police appealed on Saturday for witnesses, dashcam, CCTV, and doorbell footage from St Peter, La Pulente, L'Etacq, and nearby areas [4]. No motive or state link was named by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the diversions, cancellations, and timeline, which the BBC and the Jersey Evening Post both reported from police statements. The drone count rests on one police officer's estimate.

items.title: Moldova Restores 61 Online Public Services After Its Record Data Breach
items.lede: Moldova will accept only physical IDs at Sunday's local votes after the breach, while 21 e-government services stay offline and intrusion attempts continue.

sections.text: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency said Friday that 61 digital public services were back on the EVO portal, while 21 stay offline until security checks end [5]. The agency said attackers were still trying to break into government systems, but checks found no new data theft and no changes to state registers [5]. The 19 to 23 October attack extracted personal data of more than 750,000 citizens, and the Chișinău Municipal Prosecutor's Office has opened a criminal case [5][6]. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said authorities were examining possible foreign state involvement. A government spokesperson said the incident could be part of a broader hybrid campaign [6]. Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group [6]. Later Friday, the agency made an EVO app update mandatory to add security measures [7]. On Saturday, the Central Electoral Commission said voters in the seven localities holding new local elections and a local referendum on Sunday must show physical IDs [8]. They cannot use EVO digital documents [8]. It also suspended online filing of electoral complaints after the cyber incidents [9].

Confidence is high on the restoration figures, app update, election rules, and breach figures, reported by state agency Moldpres and, for the breach, The Record. Foreign state involvement is unconfirmed.

items.title: Dutch Police Arrest More Than Ten in The Hague Over Gen Z Protest Calls
items.lede: Riot officers briefly cleared a central street, and the city widened an emergency order before calm returned by late afternoon.

sections.text: Dutch riot police briefly cleared the Korte Voorhout in The Hague at about 15:15 on Saturday after youths ignored orders to move to the Malieveld, Omroep West reported [1]. Calls for a 'Gen Z protest' had spread on social media during the week, and shops in The Hague, Maastricht, and Amsterdam were boarded up [2]. Police said they had arrested just over ten people by about 15:30 for wearing face coverings or carrying illegal fireworks [1][2]. The city had banned face coverings for Saturday [2]. Police also arrested several protesters in Delft [2]. Several hundred people, including ADO Den Haag soccer fans, gathered on the Plein and said they had come to protect the city [1]. The city extended an emergency order to the Malieveld and the central station area in the afternoon [1]. By 16:48, both areas were almost empty [1]. Maastricht police reported no incidents, and Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht stayed quiet [2].
Confidence is high on the arrests, the riot police action, and the emergency order, reported by Omroep West and NU.nl and attributed to Dutch police and city officials.

items.title: France's Top Court Moves Paris March to Outer Boulevards as Marseille Clashes Erupt
items.lede: The Interior Ministry counted 15,000 marchers and 27 arrests by 14:00, far below last Saturday, while police fired tear gas as the Lyon march dispersed.

sections.text: France's Conseil d'État sided with the Paris police prefect overnight, canceling the Bastille–Nation route a lower court allowed Friday [3][4]. The Paris march instead ran from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton [3][5]. By 14:00, the Interior Ministry counted 15,000 marchers at 65 events and 27 arrests, against 37,000 and 217 a week earlier [5]. It called the country broadly calm [5]. In Marseille, protesters threw paving stones at riot police on Boulevard Chave, and police charged back [5]. Tensions broke out at the end of the Grenoble march, and police fired tear gas as clashes erupted when the Lyon march dispersed [5]. The prefecture's order n° 2026-01485 bars everyone from the Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles sectors from 23:00 to 06:00 on Saturday and Sunday nights [6][5][7]. The interior ministry said 83 cases had gone to the IGPN and IGGN watchdogs since mid-September, including a Reims marcher's shin seriously injured by a police grenade, franceinfo reported [8][9]. A planned 0.8% riot insurance surcharge from 2027 still needs Conseil d'État validation [10].

Confidence is high on the ruling, the 14:00 figures, and the city incidents, reported by franceinfo and by RTBF with AFP. No organizer turnout, evening toll, or Halloween-night incidents were found by the cutoff.

items.title: Italian Police Charge Students and Fire a Water Cannon in Turin During General Strike
items.lede: Police then ran 60 searches over online calls for violence, after unions claimed more than 1 million marchers and the interior ministry counted 255,000.

sections.text: Students and workers marched Friday in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna, and Naples during Italy's general strike over living costs and school funding, RTBF reported, citing AFP [11]. In Turin's Piazza Castello, police made two brief charges and used a water cannon when marchers behind shields reached the cordon protecting the prefecture. Protesters threw red-paint eggs and bottles, ANSA reported [12]. Two people were held, one of them bruised [12]. In the evening, protesters threw bottles at police in Rome and Turin, and police charged and used water cannon. USB claimed more than 1 million marchers nationwide, while the interior ministry counted 255,000 [13]. Interior Minister Piantedosi said the right to protest had been "guaranteed despite some violent people" [13]. Unions demand restored wage indexation and lower VAT on essentials, and have called another general strike for 20 November [11]. On Saturday, Italian police said they carried out 60 searches in 23 cities targeting people who urged violence at recent protests in chats and on social media [14].

Confidence is high on the strike and the Rome and Turin clashes, reported by RTBF with AFP and ANSA. Crowd figures are contested. The Turin charges and detentions rest on ANSA's account, with no police statement found by the cutoff.

items.title: Spanish Judge Jails Alleged Blocus Founder as Barcelona Braces for Halloween Night
items.lede: Catalan police set their top risk level and put more than 300 officers downtown, while arrests over online looting calls reached 10 nationwide.

sections.text: Spain's Catalan police raised their risk rating to level 4, the maximum, for Saturday's Blocus calls in Barcelona, RTVE reported [15]. It is only the second time since 2019 that police have used that level for a protest [15][16]. More than 300 officers will guard downtown Barcelona, where three gatherings were called for 17:00 and 20:00 [15]. Calls were also posted for nine other Catalan towns, including Girona, Lleida, and Mataró [15]. A court in Torrent on Saturday ordered the alleged Spanish founder of Blocus jailed after his Friday arrest in Valencia province [15]. He is under investigation for criminal organization aimed at inciting public disorder, shop burglaries, and damage [15]. Spanish police have now arrested 10 young people nationwide for urging looting, three of them in Catalonia [16]. Police also had four Telegram channels shut down, the largest with more than 3,000 members [15]. Catalan regional president Salvador Illa warned on X that anyone who comes to loot will answer to the courts [16][15]. Almería had banned face coverings, El País reported [17].

Confidence is high on the jailing, the deployment, and the arrests, reported by RTVE and La Vanguardia and consistent with earlier El País reporting. No results from the evening gatherings were found by the cutoff.

items.title: Riot Police Guard Poland's Constitutional Court After Its President Is Suspended
items.lede: President Karol Nawrocki summoned party leaders for urgent talks on Saturday, while the court's sidelined leadership calls the move a coup and Tusk defends it.

sections.text: Riot police deployed on Friday evening at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice-president, Bartłomiej Sochański, for one month. She took charge as the most senior judge, El País reported [18]. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek has asked for both judges' immunity to be lifted so they can be charged for keeping parliament-elected judges off the bench [19][18]. The court wrote on X that everyone taking part was committing the crime of a coup d'état, as Law and Justice supporters, joined by leader Jarosław Kaczyński, protested outside [19][20]. Nawrocki canceled his Senegal trip in mid-flight and went to the court at about 01:00, where video showed scuffles with judges at the entrance [19][18]. Korwin-Piotrowska has called the court's general assembly for 3 November [18]. On Saturday morning, Nawrocki's chief of staff said the president would hold urgent consultations with government and opposition parties [21]. The statement cited a threat to Poland's internal security [21].

Confidence is high on the suspension, the police deployment, the court's statement, and Nawrocki's return, reported by the BBC, El País, and ANSA. The scuffle account rests on video cited by El País. No ruling on the suspension's legality was found by the cutoff.

items.title: EU and Canada Launch an Alliance for the Future in Montreal
items.lede: Ottawa will help fund the €90 billion Ukraine loan, and a definition of associate membership, which Germany resisted, will wait for a 2027 summit.

sections.text: The EU dropped Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's offer of associate membership talks for Canada from the draft Montreal summit statement, El País and the Guardian reported [22][23]. Italy wanted the Commission's wording kept, while Germany pushed the softer formula [23]. At Friday's opening session, von der Leyen said the EU wants Canada "as close as possible to the European Union." Council President António Costa called Canada "by far the most European of the non-European countries" [24][25]. An EEAS summary says both sides will lay the groundwork for "an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself" [26]. The summit closed on Friday with an Alliance for the Future that other like-minded countries may join. Canada agreed to contribute to the €90 billion EU support loan for Ukraine, the Guardian reported [27]. Von der Leyen and Prime Minister Mark Carney both still spoke of associate membership, and leaders said its scope would be set at a 2027 summit [27].

Confidence is high on the alliance, the Ukraine loan contribution, and the 2027 timetable, reported by the Guardian and stated by EU officials. The member-state positions on the draft rest on unnamed diplomatic sourcing.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonia's Enefit Power Will Burn Shale Oil to Heat Narva From Sunday
items.lede: The state-owned firm cites high gas prices, low EU storage, and Middle East supply risks, using an exemption the environment board granted on 21 October.

sections.text: Enefit Power, part of Estonia's state-owned Eesti Energia, will start burning shale oil in the reserve boiler house of the Balti power plant on Sunday, ERR reported [1]. The switch applies when the plant's unit 11 is uncompetitive on the power market or out of service [1]. Board chairman Raine Pajo told the environment board and Climate Minister Erkki Keldo the conditions for the exemption had been met [1]. He cited price swings, rising winter demand, below-normal EU gas storage, and the risk of new gas supply disruptions under the environment board's 21 October order [1]. Pajo said the Middle East crisis pushed European gas prices to a four-year high in October [1]. He said the step is temporary and aims to keep district heating affordable for Narva residents [1].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report quoting the company's letter; no environment board response was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Latvia Bars Russian TV Host Ksenia Sobchak From Entering the Country
items.lede: Foreign Minister Baiba Braže also added Sobchak's husband, theater director Konstantin Bogomolov, to the indefinite entry ban list.

sections.text: Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže put Russian television and internet host Ksenia Sobchak on Latvia's list of unwanted persons, LSM reported Saturday [2]. Braže announced the decision on X under the Immigration Law, which lets the foreign minister decide such listings [2]. Sobchak is barred from entering Latvia indefinitely [2]. The list also now includes theater director Konstantin Bogomolov, whom LSM describes as Sobchak's husband and who once staged plays in Liepāja [2]. LSM said Latvian foreign ministers have regularly banned entertainment figures who backed the policies of aggressor states [2]. No reason specific to Sobchak was found in the report.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LSM report relaying the minister's post; the post itself was not read.

items.title: Estonia's President Picks Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask as Chancellor of Justice
items.lede: The Riigikogu must still approve Kask, who would fill the watchdog post Ülle Madise left when she became president this month.

sections.text: Estonian President Ülle Madise proposed to parliament on Saturday that Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask become the next chancellor of justice, ERR reported [3]. Madise held the post until she took office as president earlier in October [3]. She called Kask a highly regarded expert on constitutional law and fundamental rights [3]. She said the office's independence from party politics matters in the international legal community [3]. Kask was a Tallinn Circuit Court judge from 2004 to 2024 and joined the Supreme Court in September 2024 [3]. Madise consulted the parliamentary parties before naming him [3]. No vote date was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report quoting the president's statement; the statement on the president's website was not read.

items.title: Estonia's Michal Vows Not to Go Quiet on Russia Despite Reported US Pressure
items.lede: A former diplomat who recently joined the opposition Isamaa party answered that Tallinn's predictable message risks costing it seats at key tables, opening a domestic debate over tone.

sections.text: Citing four anonymous sources, Reuters reported Friday that Pentagon officials urged Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to tone down public talk of the Russian threat, LRT and BNS summarized [4]. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said the United States had made no official proposal [5]. Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov knew of no official request [6]. Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said he had no information about such appeals [4]. A top Lithuanian presidential adviser, Deividas Matulionis, said Lithuania should not deliberately provoke Russia [7]. In a longer ERR interview published Saturday, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said no such request had reached him [8][9]. He said Russia is killing women and children and that pleasing dictators or staying silent is no solution [8]. Former diplomat Jaap Ora, who recently joined the opposition Isamaa party, said Estonia's foreign policy message has become predictable [10]. Ora wrote on social media that public messages must be carefully calibrated or allies may stop inviting Estonia to key talks [10]. The Reuters original was not read.
Confidence is high on the on-record Estonian and Lithuanian statements; confidence is moderate on the US appeals themselves, which rest on anonymous sources relayed from Reuters.

items.title: Lithuania's Defense Minister Admits Savings Are Coming as Procurement Review Begins
items.lede: LRT says next year's spending is likely to fall short of a planned 5.44% of GDP, leaving about €400 million in purchase plans unfunded.

sections.text: Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas told LRT that savings will clearly have to be found and that a procurement review is under way. Cheaper alternatives to top-end systems are under consideration [11]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius is proposing 5% of GDP for defense in 2027, while State Auditor Irena Segalovičienė recalled that the earlier three-year plan set 5.44% [11]. That leaves about €400 million already in purchase plans likely to go unfunded [11]. Kaunas defended the State Defense Council's decision to delay universal male conscription to 2032, saying a faster start would lower army readiness and quality. Liberal leader Viktorija Čmilytė-Nielsen called it bad news [11]. Kaunas said nearly €2.5 billion of this year's procurement money not yet paid out is planned, with invoices due in the fourth quarter. He said a CV90 infantry fighting vehicle deal is due to be signed at the end of November [11].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LRT TV report with the minister, prime minister, and opposition on record; the auditor's figures were not checked at source.

items.title: NATO's Top Commander Tells Latvia War With Russia Is Not Inevitable
items.lede: After meeting President Rinkēvičs, General Grynkewich praised Latvia's 5% defense spending as an example every ally should follow.

sections.text: NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, General Alexus Grynkewich, said in Latvia on Friday that Russia is a threat but conflict is not inevitable. He spoke after talks with Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs, LTV reported [12]. He said allies should build resilience now and be ready, calling it "peace through strength" [12]. He said he was extremely proud that Latvia spends 5% of GDP on defense to meet capability targets ahead of schedule [12]. He called it a great example all allies should follow [12]. LTV also cited media reports that more than 70 German and Dutch generals and senior officers this week visited possible operating areas in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania [12].
Confidence is moderate: the quotes rest on one LTV report; the generals' visit is relayed from unnamed media reports and was not checked separately.

items.title: Estonian Minister Floats Closing Belarus Crossings to Halt Migrant Pressure
items.lede: Igor Taro also wants border guards cleared to use force up to lethal means, after Latvia widened its own guards' weapons powers.

sections.text: Estonian Interior Minister Igor Taro and Latvian Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava met at the Piusa border post on Friday to discuss stopping illegal migration pressure, ERR reported [13]. Both said pressure eases in winter but that effective tools were needed to make the Belarusian government stop organizing illegal migration to the Baltic states [13]. Taro said one option was for all these countries to close Belarusian border crossings for a time, noting that this had worked for Poland [13]. Dombrava said Latvia had changed its law so border guards can use weapons against people who cross illegally and target its technical infrastructure [13]. Taro said Estonian border guards should have full certainty they can use all means, up to lethal force, against hostile activity in the border zone. He said the ministry was analyzing whether Estonian law needs changes [13]. No decision to close crossings was announced.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR broadcast report quoting both ministers on record.

items.title: Albanian Police Fire Tear Gas as Tirana Protesters Throw Molotov Cocktails
items.lede: Students at the rally outside the Education Ministry turned away opposition Democratic Party lawmakers, chanting that they themselves are the opposition.

sections.text: Protesters in Albania's capital, Tirana, threw volleys of Molotov cocktails at police on Saturday, Gazeta Express reported, citing Top Channel [1]. Police answered with tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowd, and the area stayed tense [1] [2]. At a student protest outside the Education Ministry, the arrival of Democratic Party supporters and lawmakers set off a brief fight between two people, Kosovo Online reported, citing Koha [2]. Students said they wanted their movement to stay independent of parties [2]. They chanted "We are the opposition!" and "Rama to prison, Berisha to prison" [2]. No police figures for injuries or arrests were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the clashes, reported by Gazeta Express and Kosovo Online from Albanian broadcasters, with a matching ANSA headline; no official police statement was read.

items.title: Serbia's Central Bank Revokes Alta Bank's License Overnight
items.lede: The regulator also filed a criminal complaint against the lender and its officials, and insured deposits are due within seven working days.

sections.text: The National Bank of Serbia revoked Alta Bank's operating license in a statement sent to media at 02:25 CET on Saturday, Danas reported [3]. The central bank said the bank's financial condition had worsened significantly and depositors' interests were at risk [3]. The Deposit Insurance Agency will be named receiver and will pay insured amounts within seven working days [3]. Four vice governors said they learned of the bank's true condition only at an emergency board session on Friday evening, N1 reported [4]. They said it differed sharply from the reports the bank had filed [4]. The organized crime prosecutor's office said it received a criminal complaint from the central bank against Alta Bank and several officials [4]. It said it had asked the central bank on 27 October for data on the bank's foreign transfers [4]. N1 filmed police with long guns and many police vehicles outside the bank's New Belgrade headquarters [4].
Confidence is high on the license revocation and payout terms, from the central bank statement reported by Danas and N1; the central bank's own page could not be opened.

items.title: Thieves Take More Than 100 Firearms From a Warehouse in Kosovo's Gjakova
items.lede: Police have opened an investigation but have not said who owns the depot, what type of weapons are missing, or who is behind it.

sections.text: Kosovo Police said in their daily report that more than 100 firearms were stolen from a warehouse in Gjakova, N1 reported, citing KoSSev [5]. Two men reported the theft to police at about 18:00 on Friday, 30 October [5]. Police units went to the scene, the prosecutor was informed, and an investigation began [5]. The report did not name the warehouse owner or the type of weapons [5]. It also did not say how the weapons went missing [5].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the police report as relayed by KoSSev and N1; the police report itself was not read.

items.title: Italy's Defense Minister Visits Survivors of the EUFOR Chinook Crash in Bosnia
items.lede: The crash, which killed four of the 15 EUFOR personnel aboard, is the most serious air accident for international forces in Bosnia since 1997 by total casualties, Klix.ba says.

sections.text: Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto and Chief of Defense Gen. Luciano Portolano flew to Bosnia and Herzegovina with an Italian medical team, according to a EUFOR text published by Sarajevo Times [6]. They visited injured personnel at hospitals in Brčko and Tuzla [6]. EUFOR commander Maj. Gen. Maurizio Fronda and Bosnian Defense Minister Zukan Helez met them at Tuzla airport [6]. The Italian CH-47 Chinook crashed near Brčko on Thursday, killing four people and injuring 11 [6]. Sarajevo Times, citing Klix.ba, said it is the deadliest air accident for international forces in Bosnia by total casualties since a 1997 UN helicopter crash [7]. No cause had been published by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the visit and toll, from EUFOR's own text; the historical comparison rests on Klix.ba via Sarajevo Times.

items.title: Belgrade Prosecutors Probe How a Wanted Analyst Reached Serbia's RTS News
items.lede: Military analyst Aleksandar Radić, who fled abroad four months ago, used the broadcast to warn of armed party militias operating in the shadows.

sections.text: Serbia's public broadcaster RTS aired a statement on its Friday evening Dnevnik 2 by military analyst Aleksandar Radić. Radić left Serbia four months ago after being charged over his remarks about the use of a sound cannon, RTS reported [8]. Radić said armed party security units operating in parallel, men in black who were mostly armed last year, now pose a particular danger to Serbia. He said they trained at shooting ranges along the Danube and near Vršac [8]. He urged people now in government to neutralize them [8]. Belgrade's Higher Public Prosecutor's Office said the same night that Radić is wanted under a notice ordered by the Higher Court. It said he is suspected of preparing acts against Serbia's constitutional order and disclosing classified data, N1 reported [9]. It said police would be ordered to establish when, how, and with whom he arranged the statement [9]. No RTS response to the prosecutors was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high: the interview is reported by RTS itself and the prosecutors' statement by N1, with matching reports in other Serbian outlets.

items.title: NATO Says Any KFOR Troop Cuts in Kosovo Will Come Gradually
items.lede: Summing up a visit by Supreme Allied Commander Grynkewich, the force said any adjustments can be reversed if security in the region worsens.

sections.text: KFOR, NATO's Kosovo force, said Friday that any changes to its troop levels and composition will come in a measured, gradual way, Kosovo Online reported from a KFOR statement [10]. The statement summed up a visit by NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich, which it said allowed talks on streamlining KFOR. It cited a shared view that the security situation has improved [10]. Adjustments will rest on continuous assessments and can be reversed after significant security developments [10]. Grynkewich and KFOR commander Major General Roberto Vannacci met Kosovo institutions, the Serb List, and religious leaders at Gračanica Monastery [10]. No figures for planned troop changes were given.
Confidence is moderate: the statement is relayed by Kosovo Online; KFOR's own release was not opened.

items.title: Kosovo's Police Chief Quits as Femicide Protests Spread
items.lede: Justice Minister Gërvalla and Interior Minister Sveçla refused to resign even though a government report found warnings about the victim's life were ignored.

sections.text: Kosovo Police Director General Gazmend Hoxha resigned on Friday, and Prime Minister Albin Kurti accepted the resignation, according to a government statement reported by Prishtina Insight [11]. Protests demanding justice for Arlinda Zekaj, 49, killed in Vitomiricë near Peja on 25 October after reporting domestic violence, are continuing across Kosovo [11] [12]. At a joint press conference, Justice Minister Donika Gërvalla said "this is not the moment for me to resign." Interior Minister Xhelal Sveçla said their resignations would not strengthen women's protection [11]. Presenting a report ordered by Kurti, Gërvalla said institutions had received repeated and serious warnings about the threat to Zekaj's life [11]. Her former brother-in-law, Albert Sylaj, is suspected of the axe killing and is in 30-day custody [11]. Protesters outside the government building in Pristina tried to enter and were stopped by police [11]. RFE/RL said 11 police officers and two prosecutors have been suspended [12].
Confidence is high on the resignation and ministers' remarks, reported by BIRN's Prishtina Insight from a government statement and press conference, and on the protests, also reported by RFE/RL.

items.title: Bulgaria Leaves the FATF Money-Laundering Gray List After Three Years
items.lede: Prime Minister Radev says Bulgarians will stop facing extra checks and rejected transfers at foreign banks, and calls the decision a step toward OECD membership.

sections.text: The Financial Action Task Force removed Bulgaria from its list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring at its Paris plenary on Friday. Ivory Coast, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Monaco also left the list, Reuters reported via Devdiscourse [13]. The watchdog said the four countries had made progress fixing money-laundering and terrorist-financing gaps found in earlier reviews [13]. Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced the decision after Justice Minister Nikolay Naydenov informed him, Novinite reported [14]. Bulgaria was warned in 2021 and gray-listed in 2023 [14]. Radev said citizens would no longer routinely face extra scrutiny or rejected payments by foreign banks, and called the move an important step toward joining the OECD [14]. He credited legislation passed by the current parliament and said the government would keep strengthening its anti-corruption and anti-money laundering systems [14]. The FATF's own statement lists Bulgaria, Côte d'Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Monaco as no longer subject to increased monitoring [15].
Confidence is high on the removal, reported by Reuters via Devdiscourse and announced by the Bulgarian government via Novinite; Radev's claims about effects are his own.

items.title: Bulgaria's Runoff Rivals Split Over Russia in Their Only TV Debate
items.lede: Yotova pitched a Black Sea ceasefire talk including Moscow, while Gyurov called that wishful thinking and pressed for drone defenses ahead of Sunday's vote.

sections.text: Bulgaria's acting President Iliana Yotova and former caretaker premier Andrey Gyurov met Thursday on BNT in the only televised debate before the 1 November runoff [16]. Yotova proposed a meeting of the six Black Sea states to agree on a moratorium on hostilities [16] [17]. Gyurov replied, "A moratorium, expressed merely as a wish, does not constitute a defense strategy," and urged joining European drone and missile defenses [17] [16]. The election commission cleared Prime Minister Rumen Radev of election code violations by an 8-7 vote and sent complaints about his use of official channels to the National Audit Office. The Gyurov committee's appeal to the Supreme Administrative Court is pending [18] [19]. On Friday, Yotova pitched the same six-state forum, Russia included, to visiting MEPs [20]. Late Friday, former president Rosen Plevneliev and former prime ministers Boyko Borisov, Ivan Kostov, and Nikolay Denkov, joined by Sofia Mayor Vasil Terziev, backed Gyurov. Their declaration warned that the refusal to name the Russian threat in the Black Sea was raising Bulgaria's risk [21]. In final addresses before Saturday's reflection day, Yotova said voters would choose what kind of Bulgaria they want [22], and Gyurov said he wanted more responsibility, not more power [23].
Confidence is high on the debate, reported by Novinite and BGNES. BTA reported the commission ruling.

items.title: Serbia's RTS Board Accepts Director's Exit and Opens Race for Acting Chief
items.lede: Four candidates have been put forward so far for a 3 November board vote, while student protesters still reject the broadcaster's on-air apology.

sections.text: The board of Serbia's public broadcaster RTS on Friday unanimously accepted the resignation of director general Manja Grčić. It will choose a new acting director general on Tuesday, 3 November, the Journalists' Association of Serbia (UNS) said, N1 reported [24]. UNS named four nominees so far: Predrag Šarčević, Vasko Vasović, Miloš Janković, and Nikola Đinđić [24]. Before resigning, Grčić replaced news chief Bojana Mlađenović with Borivoje Uskoković, who on Thursday removed several section editors and three editors of the 19:30 Dnevnik, RTS reported [25]. False bomb threats emptied RTS buildings Thursday evening, Euronews Srbija reported [26]. A statement from the new editorial board, read on air, called the changes a "first measure of apology," and Students in Blockade replied that they accept "only resignations" [27]. Student List candidate Mirjana Nikolić also demanded the resignation of Dejan Jovanović over selective reporting, RTS reported [28]. RTS later published the board's statement: it noted Grčić's resignation and invited eligible employees to apply by 17:00 on Monday, 2 November. It said deputy director general Dejan Jovanović will run the broadcaster until an acting chief is named [29].
Confidence is moderate: the board decision and nominees rest on UNS via N1; the editor changes come from RTS itself, and the bomb threats and student reply from Euronews Srbija.

items.title: Armenia Starts Issuing Biometric Passports, With Pashinyan the First Applicant
items.lede: A private partner, HayPass, runs the new centers; officials promise 23 offices nationwide by early 2027 and documents within 14 working days.

sections.text: Armenia launched a new biometric passport and ID card system on Saturday, Armenpress reported [1]. Private company HayPass opened its first service center at a Yerevan mall [1]. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was the first visitor and gave his own biometric data [1]. Interior Minister Arpine Sargsyan said the system would end identity theft [1]. She said the partnership compressed seven to eight years of work into about a year [1]. Applicants must pre-register online, and a passport costs 28,650 drams [1]. Twelve regional offices open on Monday, with 23 planned by the first quarter of 2027 [1].
Confidence is moderate: the details rest on Armenpress, the state news agency, which reported from the opening; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Azerbaijan Welcomes Turkey's Nominee for UN Secretary-General
items.lede: Baku's warm words for OSCE chief Sinirlioğlu come after Aliyev skipped Friday's Turkic summit in Ankara amid strained ties.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry welcomed Turkey's nomination of Feridun Sinirlioğlu, now secretary general of the OSCE, as UN secretary-general, APA and Trend reported [2] [3]. Spokesperson Aykhan Hajizada answered a media question on Saturday [2]. He said the choice should rest on candidates' qualifications, diplomatic experience, impartiality, and ability to build consensus [2] [3]. He said consultations among member states should produce a decision that makes the UN more effective [3]. Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev skipped the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara on Friday amid strained ties, as reported in earlier editions. No Turkish reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the statement, carried by APA and Trend from the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry; the link to the summit row is context, not stated by Baku.

items.title: UN Biodiversity Talks Hosted by Armenia End With the 'Yerevan Pathway'
items.lede: Delegates negotiated for about 12 hours from Friday night into Saturday morning to adopt roughly 50 decisions, though splits over nature finance persisted.

sections.text: More than 100 countries reached agreements at the COP17 UN biodiversity conference in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, Xinhua reported [4]. The final session ran about 12 hours, from Friday night into Saturday morning [4]. Delegates adopted the Yerevan Pathway to speed up action toward the 2030 nature targets [4]. It calls for stronger national plans, better monitoring, and more financing [4]. Divisions over finance, harmful subsidies, and scientific evidence remained [4]. Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan, the conference president, said about 50 decisions were adopted [5] [4]. Parties chose Quito, Ecuador, to host COP18 in 2028 [4].
Confidence is high, from Xinhua's on-site report and Armenpress coverage of the president's news conference; the convention secretariat's own text was not read.

items.title: Fitch Lifts Georgia's Credit Outlook to Positive but Keeps the BB Rating
items.lede: The agency credits fast-growing foreign reserves, a low current account deficit, and growth that averaged above 8% from 2023 to 2025.

sections.text: Fitch Ratings kept Georgia's sovereign credit rating at BB on 30 October and changed the outlook from stable to positive, RFE/RL's Georgian service reported, citing the Finance Ministry [6]. The rating has not changed in three years [6]. Fitch cited rapid reserve growth, a low current account deficit, and high growth, which averaged above 8% from 2023 to 2025 [6]. It also cited prudent fiscal policy, moderate government debt, and a stable banking system [6]. Fitch said Georgia keeps growing strongly despite higher geopolitical risks and energy prices [6]. Fitch's own release was not read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on RFE/RL's Georgian service relaying the Finance Ministry; a Trend report was paywalled.

items.title: Armenian Prosecutors Take Up a Complaint Against Russia's Railway Operator
items.lede: An Armenian party leader wants a criminal probe of the Russian Railways subsidiary that has run the country's rail network since 2008.

sections.text: Armenia's Prosecutor General's Office accepted for consideration a complaint against South Caucasus Railway, JAMnews reported [7]. The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Russian Railways [7]. Republic Party leader Aram Sargsyan filed the complaint [7]. He asked prosecutors to examine dismantled track, falling freight volumes, and unmet investment duties [7]. He asked them to open a criminal case if they find abuses [7]. Armenia has proposed moving the 30-year concession, signed in 2008, to a third party, but Moscow has not agreed [7]. A joint working group set up two weeks ago has three months to report [7].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on JAMnews; the prosecutor's brief statement was not read directly.

items.title: Germany's Merz Agrees Closer Defense Ties With South Korea on Asia Trip
items.lede: The chancellor said he will count on Asian partners' support when the coalition backing Ukraine meets in Berlin in November.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz ended a five-day trip to Singapore, Japan, and South Korea on Saturday [1] [2]. He stressed the importance of trade with all three countries [2] [1]. Merz agreed with South Korea to expand defense cooperation, including on cybersecurity [1]. He said Germany wants to build a network of mid-sized partners to balance major powers such as China and the United States [1]. North Korean soldiers fighting for Russia in Ukraine came up in his talks in all three capitals [1]. Merz said he would count on their support in the coalition of the willing, which he has invited to meet in Berlin in November [1]. He also visited Panmunjom on the border between the two Koreas [1].
Confidence is moderate. The defense and Ukraine details rest on one tagesschau report from the traveling press. Deutschlandfunk confirms only that the trip ended with a focus on trade.

items.title: Germany's Gen Z Rallies Draw Thousands, Far Fewer Than Organizers Expected
items.lede: Police stopped marches in Cologne and Stuttgart over masked participants and pyrotechnics, while Berlin police counted about 5,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate.

sections.text: Germany's 'Gen Z regelt' youth rallies went ahead Saturday afternoon in dozens of cities, but turnout fell well short of organizers' expectations [3] [4]. About 160,000 people had pledged to take part beforehand [5] [4]. Berlin police counted about 5,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate, while organizers claimed 10,000 [4] [6]. Police counted 1,800 in Munich and about 1,000 in Frankfurt, according to dpa [4]. Leipzig and Dresden each drew several thousand people [3] [4]. Cologne police canceled the march after some participants masked their faces and set off pyrotechnics, and the event continued as a stationary rally [3] [6]. In Stuttgart, police halted the march over masked participants, smoke pots, and firecrackers and told marchers to keep to the agreed route [7]. Duesseldorf police made four arrests and were checking whether they were linked to the protests [6]. Before the rallies, Germany's Interior Ministry said federal police would turn back violent foreign protesters at the border [5] [8]. The SPD's parliamentary group called for a national education summit in response [4]. Police said the rallies stayed peaceful at first in the four cities run by the initiative [4].
Confidence is high on turnout figures and police actions, drawn from police statements reported by Deutschlandfunk, dpa, and WDR. No final nationwide count was available by the cutoff.

items.title: German Police Examine Left-Wing Claim Over Arson at Rheinmetall Drone Site
items.lede: A posting on a platform rated as extremist by intelligence officials claims Friday's fire at the Hesse construction site, and police say they are examining it closely.

sections.text: German police said Saturday they are examining a claim of responsibility for Friday's arson at a construction site near Kassel, where Rheinmetall plans a drone center [9]. The claim appeared on an online platform that Germany's domestic intelligence agency classifies as left-wing extremist [9]. Three construction machines burned at the former Kassel-Calden airfield early Friday, and police believe the fire was set on purpose [9]. The state security police unit is investigating a suspected political motive [9]. Police are still seeking witnesses and have not given a damage estimate [9]. Rheinmetall is investing more than 260 million euros in Kassel and Calden for logistics and drone testing, and the state of Hesse is adding 25 million euros [9].
Confidence is moderate. Police confirm the claim exists but have not judged whether it is authentic. The account rests on hessenschau, with the same dpa report carried by other outlets.

items.title: Germany's Wadephul Rules Out Normal Ties With Russia After G20 Photo Snub
items.lede: The foreign minister says serious Russia–Ukraine talks could come soon if the West stays firm, while Lavrov mocked what he called Europe's family-photo diplomacy.

sections.text: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said there is "no normality with Russia" after the G20 ministers' traditional group photo in Atlanta was canceled [10] [11]. European ministers had refused to pose with Russia's Sergei Lavrov [10] [11]. Wadephul told Deutschlandfunk that serious talks between Russia and Ukraine could come soon if the West takes a firm, clear line with Moscow [11]. He said Lavrov's attendance showed Moscow was willing to face criticism from other countries [11]. Lavrov said Russia's position on Ukraine has not changed [10] [11]. He accused the Europeans of trying to meddle in the peace process and called their stance an "arrogant boycott" and family-photo diplomacy [10] [11]. No joint final statement is expected, and the ministers meet Saturday to discuss supply chains [10].
Confidence is high on the remarks and the canceled photo. Both tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk reported them, and Wadephul spoke on the record to Deutschlandfunk and ZDF.

items.title: IG Metall Calls First Warning Strikes in Germany's Metal and Electrical Industry
items.lede: The union says walkouts will hit a major Bavarian carmaker on Monday as it pushes for a 5% raise against employers' offer of 1.3% from July 2028.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union has called the first warning strikes of the metal and electrical industry's pay dispute for this weekend, with overnight walkouts and rallies [12]. The union said a large Bavarian carmaker will be hit for the first time on Monday [12]. IG Metall wants a 5% raise, while employers are offering one-off payments from the middle of next year and a 1.3% raise from July 2028 [12]. The industry employs 3.7 million people nationwide [12]. A split complicates the talks: carmakers and their suppliers are struggling, while the arms and electronics sector is booming, and the union wants workers to share in its profits [12].
Confidence is moderate because it rests on a single Deutschlandfunk report of the union's plans. Strike locations and turnout were not given by the cutoff.
